items.title: Eight Weekly Stages of the Foetus

items.zh: 若經七月、六月，不名圓滿，或復缺減。又此胎藏六處位中，由母所食生麁津味而得資長。於羯羅藍等微細位中，由微細津味資長應知。
items.en: If only seven or six months have passed, this is not called complete, and may even be called deficient. Further, once the foetus reaches the stage of the sense-faculties, it is nourished by the coarser nutrient fluid the mother consumes; in the subtler stages, from the kalala onward, it should be understood to be nourished by a subtler nutrient fluid.

items.zh: 復次，此之胎藏，八位差別。何等為八？謂羯羅藍位、遏部曇位、閉尸位、鍵南位、鉢羅賒佉位、髮毛爪位、根位、形位。
items.en: Further, this foetus passes through eight distinct stages. What are the eight? The kalala stage; the arbuda stage; the peśī stage; the ghana stage; the praśākhā stage; the stage of hair, down, and nails; the stage of the sense-faculties; and the stage of bodily form.

items.zh: 若已結凝，箭內仍稀，名羯羅藍。若表裏如酪，未至肉位，名遏部曇。若已成肉，仍極柔軟，名閉尸。若已堅厚，稍堪摩觸，名為鍵南。即此肉摶增長，支分相現，名鉢羅賒佉。從此以後，髮毛爪現，即名此位。從此以後，眼等根生，名為根位。從此以後，彼所依處分明顯現，名為形位。
items.en: When it has just curdled, still thin within like an arrow-wound, this is called the kalala stage. When, outside and within, it is like curdled milk, but not yet flesh, this is called the arbuda stage. When it has become flesh, but is still extremely soft, this is called the peśī stage. When it has become firm and thick, able to bear some slight touch, this is called the ghana stage. When this mass of flesh grows further and the marks of the limbs appear, this is called the praśākhā stage. From this point, when hair, down, and nails appear, this very stage is so named. From this point, when the eye and the other faculties arise, this is called the stage of the sense-faculties. From this point, when the physical supports of these faculties become clearly manifest, this is called the stage of form.

items.zh: 又於胎藏中，或由先業力，或由其母不避不平等力所生隨順風故，令此胎藏或髮、或色、或皮及餘支分變異而生。髮變異生者，謂由先世所作能感此惡不善業，及由其母多習灰鹽等味若飲、若食，令此胎藏髮毛稀尠。
items.en: Further, within the womb, whether through the force of past karma, or through a wind arising from the mother's failure to avoid what is out of balance, the foetus's hair, complexion, skin, or other bodily parts may develop abnormally. Abnormal hair arises through unwholesome karma from a past life capable of bringing about this result, and through the mother's habitual consumption of ash- or salt-flavoured food or drink, causing the foetus's hair to become sparse.

items.zh: 色變異生者，謂由先業因，如前說，及由其母習近煖熱現在緣故，令彼胎藏黑黯色生。又母習近極寒室等，令彼胎藏極白色生。又由其母多噉熱食，令彼胎藏極赤色生。
items.en: Abnormal complexion arises through the same kind of past karma, and through the mother's habitual exposure to warmth and heat, causing the foetus's complexion to darken; or through her habitual exposure to extreme cold, causing it to become extremely pale; or through her eating much hot food, causing it to become extremely ruddy.

items.zh: 皮變異生者，謂由宿業因，如前說，及由其母多習婬欲現在緣故，令彼胎藏或癬、疥、癩等惡皮而生。支分變異生者，謂由先業因，如前說，及由其母多習馳走、跳躑威儀，及不避不平等現在緣故，令彼胎藏諸根支分缺減而生。
items.en: Abnormal skin arises through the same kind of past karma, and through the mother's habitual indulgence in sexual activity, causing the foetus to develop conditions such as ringworm, scabies, or a leprous skin. Abnormalities of the limbs arise through the same kind of past karma, and through the mother's habitual running, jumping, and other unbalanced conduct in the present, causing the foetus's faculties and limbs to be deficient or incomplete.

items.zh: 又彼胎藏，若當為女，於母左脇，倚脊向腹而住。若當為男，於母右脇，倚腹向脊而住。
items.en: Further, if the foetus is to be female, it dwells on the mother's left side, its back against her spine, facing her belly. If it is to be male, it dwells on the mother's right side, its back against her belly, facing her spine.

items.zh: 又此胎藏極成滿時，其母不堪持此重胎，內風便發，生大苦惱。又此胎藏業報所發生分風起，令頭向下、足便向上，胎衣纏裹而趣產門。其正出時，胎衣遂裂，分之兩腋。出產門時，名正生位。
items.en: Further, when the foetus reaches its full term, the mother's body can no longer bear to carry this heavy burden, and an internal wind arises within her, bringing great distress. Further, a wind proper to the process of birth, brought about by the ripening of karma, then arises, turning the foetus's head downwards and its feet upwards; wrapped in the birth-membrane, it moves towards the birth canal. As it is actually born, the birth-membrane splits open along both sides. The moment it emerges from the birth canal is called the stage of actual birth.

items.title: The Seven Stages of Growing Up

items.zh: 生後漸次觸生分觸，所謂眼觸乃至意觸。次復隨墮施設事中，所謂隨學世事言說。次復耽著家室，謂長大種類故，諸根成就故。
items.en: After birth, one gradually comes into contact proper to this stage of existence — that is, contact through the eye, and so on up to contact through the mind. Next, one falls into the conventions of the world, learning to speak and act as the world does. Next, one becomes attached to household life, as one's kind matures and one's faculties ripen.

items.zh: 次造諸業，謂起世間工巧業處。次復受用境界，所謂色等若可愛、不可愛。受此苦樂，謂由先業因，或由現在緣。隨緣所牽，或往五趣，或向涅槃。
items.en: Next, one takes up various occupations — the skilled trades of the world. Next, one makes use of objects — forms and the rest — whether pleasant or unpleasant. One experiences pleasure and pain from these, whether through the force of past karma or through present conditions. And, drawn along by these very conditions, one proceeds either to the five realms of rebirth, or towards nirvāṇa.

items.title: Four Ways Others Sustain a New Life

items.zh: 又諸有情，隨於如是有情類中自體生時，彼有情類於此有情作四種緣。謂種子所引故，食所資養故，隨逐守護故，隨學造作身語業故。
items.en: Further, whenever a being is born within any kind of beings, other beings of that same kind provide four conditions for this new being: being drawn forth by their generative seed; being nourished by the food they provide; being followed and protected by them; and being taught by them how to act and speak.

items.zh: 初謂父母精血所引。次彼生已，知其所欲，方求飲食而用資長。次常隨逐，專志守護，不令起作非時之行及不平等行。
items.en: The first is being drawn forth by the parents' generative fluid. Next, once born, those who know what the child needs seek out food to nourish and sustain it. Next, they constantly attend to it, dedicatedly protecting it, so that it does not act at an improper time or in a way that is out of balance.

items.title: An Endless Relay — and Why It Is So Hard to See Through

items.zh: 次令習學世俗言說等事。由長大種類故，諸根成就故，此復於餘，此復於餘。如是展轉，諸有情類無始時來受苦受樂，未曾獲得出苦樂法，乃至諸佛未證菩提。若從他聞音，及內正思惟，由如是故，方得漏盡。
items.en: Next, they teach the child the world's conventional speech and other such matters. As this being grows, matures, and its faculties ripen, it in turn does the very same for another, who in turn does the same for yet another. Turning on in this way, beings have, since beginningless time, experienced pleasure and pain without ever finding a way beyond pleasure and pain — until the Buddhas attain awakening. It is only by hearing the teaching from another, and by rightly reflecting within, that one finally attains the exhaustion of the defilements.

items.zh: 如是句義甚為難悟。謂我無有若分、若誰、若事，我亦都非若分、若誰、若事。
items.en: This very point is exceedingly difficult to realise: that the self has no temporal portion, no enduring someone, and no possessed thing; and that the self, likewise, is not itself any portion, any someone, or any thing.

items.title: The Fifteenth Power Begins: The World's Destruction

items.zh: 如是略說內分死生已。云何外分若壞若成？謂由諸有情所作能感成壞業故。
items.en: Thus has the inner aspect — death and birth — been briefly explained. What now is the outer aspect: its destruction and its formation? It comes about through karma created by beings, capable of bringing about the world's formation and destruction.

items.zh: 若有能感壞業現前，爾時便有外壞緣起，由彼外分皆悉散壞，非如內分由壽量盡。何以故？由一切外分所有麁色，四大所成，恒相續住，非如內分。
items.en: When the karma capable of bringing about destruction actually manifests, the outer condition for destruction then arises, and the outer world is entirely dispersed and destroyed — unlike the inner aspect, which ends through the exhaustion of a lifespan. Why is this? Because all the coarse matter of the outer world, made of the four great elements, remains in unbroken continuity for far longer than does the inner aspect.

items.zh: 又感成器世間業，此業決定能引劫住，不增不減。
items.en: Further, the karma that brings the physical world into formation is fixed in its power to sustain it for a full eon — neither more nor less.

blocks.text: Today completes the inner account of birth and turns outwards. The treatise describes the eight weekly stages of the embryo, what makes a foetus develop abnormally, its position in the womb, birth, the seven stages of growing up, and the four ways others sustain a new life. Then comes a short but profound sentence on non-self, and the start of the "outer" side of the mental consciousness's powers: the destruction and formation of the world.

One stage per week, as Master Cháng Bǎi explains: **kalala** (羯羅藍, thin, "like an arrow-wound" within), **arbuda** (遏部曇, like curdled milk, not yet flesh; Venerable Miào Jìng: "blister"), **peśī** (閉尸, flesh, but very soft, like butter), **ghana** (鍵南, firm enough to bear a slight touch, a lump of flesh), **praśākhā** (鉢羅賒佉, the limbs appear), then hair, down, and nails; the sense-faculties; and bodily form.

The last two repeat a distinction from Day 1. At the faculty stage the invisible pure-form faculties arise; at the form stage their visible "supporting organs" appear. Venerable Miào Jìng: "At the faculty stage the five pure-form faculties appear; at the form stage the supporting organs appear too."

Hair, complexion, skin, and limbs may develop abnormally "through the force of past karma, or through a wind arising from the mother's failure to avoid what is out of balance": too much heat, cold, hot food, salty food, and so on. Master Cháng Bǎi reads every case as two factors working together: past karma sets the tendency, and the mother's conduct triggers it. His modern example of excessive cold is a fondness for air-conditioning. Venerable Miào Jìng goes further: even the mother's imbalance is, in the end, connected with the child's own karma.

A female foetus lies on the mother's left, a male on her right. At full term two winds arise: one in the mother, bringing distress, and a "wind proper to birth", produced by the child's own ripening karma, which turns it head downwards towards the birth-canal. Even the mechanics of birth are described in terms of karma.

After birth come: contact through the six senses; "falling into the conventions of the world" (Venerable Miào Jìng: 墮 here means "entering", not moral decline; one learns to speak and act as the world does); attachment to household life; work and trades; enjoyment of objects; pleasure and pain; and finally, "drawn along by these very conditions", heading either to the five realms of rebirth or towards nirvāṇa.

Master Cháng Bǎi asks why the same ordinary life leads some to rebirth and others to nirvāṇa. His answer: it depends on whether one hears the true teaching and reflects rightly on the very same pleasure and pain, seeing that there is no real self to whom it happens.

subs.head: Four ways others sustain a life

blocks.text: Beings of the same kind give a newborn four things: generation, food, protection, and teaching. And the newborn will one day do the same for another, "turning on in this way" since beginningless time. Master Cháng Bǎi draws a familiar Mahāyāna conclusion: over so long a saṃsāra, every being may once have been our father or mother, which is a basis for goodwill towards all.

subs.head: Why the way out is hard to see

blocks.text: Beings have experienced pleasure and pain without end, and only "by hearing the teaching from another, and by rightly reflecting within" do they reach the end of the defilements. Venerable Miào Jìng: both are needed, the outer condition and the inner work. (This repeats the point of Day 1's commentary on "hearing from others".)

Then comes a sentence worth memorising: "This very point is exceedingly difficult to realise: that the self has no temporal portion, no enduring someone, and no possessed thing; and that the self, likewise, is not itself any portion, any someone, or any thing." Both teachers explain 分 ("portion") as time: in past, present, and future, no self can be found. They differ slightly on the other two words; Venerable Miào Jìng takes "someone" (誰) as noble or ordinary beings and "thing" (事) as the aggregates, bases, and elements. However read, the point is that neither within experience nor as anything apart from it is there a self.

subs.head: The outer world: formed and destroyed by karma

blocks.text: "Thus has the inner aspect, death and birth, been briefly explained. What now is the outer aspect?" The world, too, comes about "through karma created by beings". Venerable Miào Jìng: a living body comes from individual karma (不共業), the shared world from shared karma (共業). Master Cháng Bǎi explains why this belongs among the powers of the mental consciousness: making karma is its special function, so the world's formation and destruction are its work too.

The difference between inner and outer is instructive. A life ends when its lifespan is used up; the world ends when the karma that sustains it is exhausted and the "outer condition for destruction" arises. The karma that forms the world sustains it for exactly one eon, "neither more nor less".

quiz.q: What is the correct order of the eight stages of the foetus?
options: kalala, peśī, arbuda, ghana, sense-faculties, form, praśākhā, hair-down-nails
kalala, arbuda, peśī, ghana, praśākhā, hair-down-nails, sense-faculties, form
arbuda, kalala, ghana, peśī, form, sense-faculties, hair-down-nails, praśākhā
kalala, arbuda, peśī, form, sense-faculties, ghana, hair-down-nails, praśākhā
quiz.why: "The kalala stage; the arbuda stage; the peśī stage; the ghana stage; the praśākhā stage; the stage of hair, down, and nails; the stage of the sense-faculties; and the stage of bodily form." Master Cháng Bǎi: one stage per week. Venerable Miào Jìng's glosses: arbuda means "blister" (like thick curds), peśī is like butter, ghana means "firm and thick" (a lump of flesh), praśākhā means "limbs."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why may a foetus's hair, complexion, skin, or limbs develop abnormally?
options: only because of the father's karma
only because of the stars
through the force of past karma, or through a wind arising from the mother's failure to avoid what is out of balance
purely by chance
quiz.why: "Whether through the force of past karma, or through a wind arising from the mother's failure to avoid what is out of balance, the foetus's hair, complexion, skin, or other bodily parts may develop abnormally." The *Pixunji*: what past karma brings is "ripening outflow," what present conditions produce is "nourishment outflow," and both arise by way of wind. Venerable Miào Jìng explains "the wind that accords": the result cannot act on its own; it follows its cause.

quiz.q: Among the seven stages of growing up, what does "falling into the conventions of the world" refer to?
options: falling into the three unhappy realms
becoming attached to household life
learning the world's conventional speech — learning to speak and act as the world does
taking up the skilled trades of the world
quiz.why: "Next, one falls into the conventions of the world, learning to speak and act as the world does." Venerable Miào Jìng: "墮 means to enter" — not falling into ruin, but entering into the world's conventions. The *Pixunji*: the three worldly affairs and four kinds of speech are what the world sets up, called its conventions; learning them is "falling into" them. A misreads 墮 as moral decline. B and D are the third and fourth stages.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what four conditions do beings of the same kind provide for a newborn being?
options: the causal, immediately-preceding, object, and dominant conditions
generosity, kind speech, beneficial action, and cooperation
food, clothing, shelter, and transport
being drawn forth by their generative seed, being nourished by food they provide, being followed and protected, and being taught how to act and speak
quiz.why: "Being drawn forth by their generative seed; being nourished by the food they provide; being followed and protected by them; and being taught by them how to act and speak." A names the four conditions of Abhidharma, which are not what is meant here. From this Master Cháng Bǎi draws the point that over such a long saṃsāra, "every man and woman may once have been one's father or mother" — a basis for goodwill rather than hostility.

quiz.q: The treatise says beings have experienced pleasure and pain since beginningless time without finding a way out. By what means is the exhaustion of the defilements finally attained?
options: by austerities alone
by being raised by one's parents
by hearing the teaching from another, and by rightly reflecting within
by meditative absorption alone
quiz.why: "It is only by hearing the teaching from another, and by rightly reflecting within, that one finally attains the exhaustion of the defilements." Venerable Miào Jìng: "One is 'hearing from another,' the other 'right reflection within'" — both forces are needed. He names two reasons beings keep cycling: lacking the decisive condition (not hearing the teaching), and the meaning being hard to realise (non-self is not easily understood).

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what brings about the destruction and formation of the outer world, and how does this differ from the death of the inner aspect?
options: by the outer world's own lifespan running out, just as with a person
by Mahābrahmā's will
by karma created by beings, capable of bringing about formation and destruction; the outer world is dispersed and destroyed, unlike the inner aspect, which ends through the exhaustion of a lifespan
purely natural, unrelated to karma
quiz.why: "It comes about through karma created by beings, capable of bringing about the world's formation and destruction. When the karma capable of bringing about destruction actually manifests, the outer condition for destruction then arises … unlike the inner aspect, which ends through the exhaustion of a lifespan." Venerable Miào Jìng: a living body comes from individual karma, the world from shared karma. B is exactly the misconception §31 dispels — Mahābrahmā is no creator.
